texts.preamble: Mahesh Chander @ Mahesh Chand vs State Of Haryana on 18 March, 2019 Author: Ramendra Jain Bench: Ramendra Jain -1- Crr-3908 of 2013 (O&M) In The High Court Of Punjab And Haryana At Chandigarh Crr-3908 of 2013 (O&M) Date of Decision: 18.03.2019 Mahesh Chander @ Mahesh Chand ....Petitioner Versus State of Haryana ....Respondent Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Ramendra Jain Present:- Mr. Aditya Sanghi, Advocate, for the petitioner. Mr. Raj Kumar Makkar, Sr. Dag, Haryana. Ramendra Jain, J. (Oral)
texts.facts: Briefly, on 10.05.2001 Government Food Inspector purchased 750 grams of 'dal moong dhuli' out of total quantity of 15 kg kept by the petitioner for sale, on payment of requisite price and converted into three separate parcels, out of which one was sent to Public Analyst, Haryana, Chandigarh, who vide his report dated 11.05.2001 declared the sample mis- branded on account of its coating with tartrazine (a synthetic food colour). Mahesh Chander @ Mahesh Chand vs State Of Haryana on 18 March, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14773498/ 1 Consequently, Government 1 of 4 Food Inspector filed a complaint CRR-3908 of 2013 (O&M) against the petitioner, who after holding trial was convicted and sentenced in the manner as narrated above in the opening part of the judgment. Being aggrieved, petitioner preferred appeal, but remained unsuccessful, as the same too was dismissed by the Appellate Court vide judgment dated 04.12.2013.
texts.arguments: Learned counsel for the petitioner drawing attention of this Court towards Rule 28 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 (in short the 'Rules') inter alia contends that both the Courts below have failed to appreciate that addition of tatrazine in 'dal moong dhuli' does not tentamount to food adulteration. Therefore, without compliance of Section 16-A of the Act, petitioner could not have been convicted. In support of his contention, learned counsel placed reliance on the judgment of this Court in Hari Ram v. State of Haryana, (2009) 5 RCR (Criminal) 561. On the other hand, learned State counsel refuting above submissions and pleading legality and validity of the impugned judgments of both the Courts below, referring to Rule 48-A of the Rules urged that petitioner could not have kept 'dal moong dhuli' coloured with tatrazine without any permit or licence, which the petitioner could not produce at any stage. Having given thoughtful consideration to the rival submissions, this Court finds the instant revision completely devoid of any merit for the reasons to follow. Petitioner cannot be given benefit of Rule 28 for violating Rule 48 of the Rules, by keeping coloured 'dal moong dhuli' without any permit or licence. While exercising its revisional powers, this Court has very limited 2 of 4 CRR-3908 of 2013 (O&M) jurisdiction, which can only be exercised, (i) when the Courts below have acted beyond jurisdiction vested in them or (ii) have not exercised the same diligently and (iii) have exercised illegally. Learned counsel for the petitioner has not been able to show any such infirmities in the judgments of both the Courts below. Petitioner was tried, treating complaint of the Government Food Inspector as a warrant case in which there is always more scope for an accused to rebut the evidence of the prosecution by leading evidence in defence unlike summary case, inasmuch as in a warrant case after recording statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. an accused is afforded opportunity to lead his evidence in defence, if any. Therefore, petitioner on technical ground of non-compliance of Section 16-A of the Act cannot be acquitted by setting aside two judgments of both the Courts below based on appreciation of evidence. At this stage, learned counsel referring to the judgment of this Court in Manbir Singh v. State of Haryana (CRR-1237 of 2012) decided on 01.12.2018, prays for reducing the sentence of the petitioner on the ground that this criminal trial is hanging on his head like damocle's sword for more than fifteen years, which is a sufficient mitigating circumstance to treat him 3 of 4 CRR-3908 of 2013 (O&M) leniently. Petitioner has suffered the ordeal for a long period and has already undergone sentence for one month and eight days.
